adjudication.evidence: Original observations show a sustained ~10 MAD drop in N/E/U around index 489–517, followed by a clear return to pre-event levels by index 520. Both P1 and P2 span nearly identical intervals (487–518 and 489–517), but the interior (e.g., indices 495–510) shows persistent offset without recovery within the interval—indicating a single temporary platform, not two overlapping ones. The residual plots confirm that subtracting either onset offset restores continuity across all axes, with no residual step inside the interval. No independent permanent step is present inside; the earlier jump at ~485 is separate and precedes the platform. Thus only one genuine temporary platform exists, best represented by the tighter, observation-supported range 489–517 (P2).
